title: Food Chains and Food Webs
seo_title: Primary 6 Science: Food Chains and Food Webs Worksheets (PSLE Practice with Answers)
standard_code: Primary 6: Interactions within the environment (Food chains and food webs)
standard_text: Identify producers, consumers (herbivores, carnivores, omnivores), predators and prey, and decomposers. Trace energy from the Sun through food chains and food webs, and predict how a change in one population affects others in a food web (summary of the MOE Primary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Primary 6 science worksheets for Singapore pupils on food chains and food webs: producers, consumers, predators and prey, and changes in populations in mangrove, garden, pond and reef webs. PSLE practice with answers.
key_big: Arrows show where the energy goes.
key_sub: Producers start every food chain; consumers eat them.
body_html:
How to think about it

A food chain shows what eats what. The arrow points from the food to the eater, the way energy flows.

  • Energy comes from the Sun. Producers (plants) make food.
  • Consumers: herbivores eat plants, carnivores eat animals, omnivores eat both. Predators hunt prey.
  • A food web is many food chains linked together.
  • If one population changes, others in the web change too. Decomposers recycle dead matter.
Example

In 'algae → snail → mudskipper → kingfisher', what eats the snail?

Follow the arrow from the snail

Answer: The mudskipper.

Example

If all the mudskippers die, what happens to kingfishers that eat only mudskippers?

They lose their food

Answer: Their number decreases.

Common mistakes

  • Reading the arrow as 'eats' and pointing it at the food.
  • Calling the Sun a producer. The Sun is the source of energy; plants are producers.
  • Thinking removing a top predator has no effect. Its prey may increase.
  • Forgetting decomposers, which return nutrients to the soil.

faq.q: Which way does the arrow point in a food chain?
faq.a: From the food to the animal that eats it. It shows the direction energy flows.

faq.q: What is the difference between a food chain and a food web?
faq.a: A food chain is one path of feeding. A food web is many food chains linked together.

faq.q: What happens if one animal in a food web is removed?
faq.a: Its prey may increase, and the animals that eat it may decrease, especially if they have no other food.

c: several food chains that are linked together
items.e: Most animals eat more than one kind of food.

a living thing that hunts and eats other animals

items.q: Food chain: pondweed → tadpole → water beetle → heron. Which is the producer?
items.e: The producer makes its own food using sunlight; it is always first.

items.q: Why does a food chain always start with a plant (or other producer)?

items.e: Producers come first.

items.e: Herbivores eat only plants, carnivores only animals, omnivores both.

items.q: What would happen to a food web if all the producers died?
c: All the consumers would eventually die from lack of food.
items.e: Every chain starts with a producer.

items.q: Can an animal be both a predator and prey?
c: Yes. A mudskipper eats snails but is eaten by kingfishers.
items.e: Many animals are both.

items.q: Which statement about energy in a food chain is correct?
c: Energy is created by each animal.
Energy passes from the top predator to the plant.
Energy passes from the producer to the consumers.
items.e: It flows in the direction of the arrows.

items.q: Look at the food web of a coral reef. In this web, the zooplankton eats phytoplankton. What kind of consumer is it?
items.e: Herbivores eat only plants, carnivores only animals, omnivores both.

items.q: An animal eats only plants. What is it called?
items.e: Herbivores are plant-eaters.

items.e: The frog hunts and eats the snail.

items.e: The shark hunts and eats the squid.

items.e: Each arrow points from the food to the animal that eats it.

items.q: Why are food webs more realistic than single food chains?
c: Plants eat animals in food webs.
Most animals eat more than one kind of food and are eaten by more than one animal.
items.e: Food webs show many links.

items.q: Look at the food web of a pond. Which food chain is part of this food web?
items.e: Each arrow points from the food to the animal that eats it.

items.e: The squid hunts and eats the small fish.

items.q: Why are decomposers important in a food web?
c: They break down dead matter and return nutrients to the soil for plants.
items.e: Nutrients are recycled.

items.q: Look at the food web of a school garden. In this web, the mynah eats caterpillars and grasshoppers. What kind of consumer is it?
items.e: Herbivores eat only plants, carnivores only animals, omnivores both.

items.q: An animal eats both plants and animals. What is it called?
items.e: Omni- means all.

items.q: Why are there usually more producers than top consumers?
c: Top consumers make their own food.
Energy is lost at each step, so less energy reaches the top.
items.e: Only part of the energy is passed on.

c: There would probably be fewer phytoplankton.

items.q: Food chain: phytoplankton → krill → whale. If the number of phytoplankton fell, what would most likely happen to the krill?
c: There would be less food, so their numbers would fall.
items.e: Animals depend on what they eat.

items.q: Look at the food web of a coral reef. Which of these does the small fish eat?
items.e: The arrow points from the food to the small fish.

items.q: Owls cough up pellets of bones and fur. What can scientists learn from them?
c: what the owl has been eating
items.e: Evidence of diet.

items.q: Look at the food web of a coral reef. Most of the sharks are removed. Which population is most likely to increase at first?
items.e: Only the shark eats squid in this web, so fewer of them are eaten.

items.q: Look at the food web of a school garden. Most of the snakes are removed. Which population is most likely to increase at first?
items.e: Only the snake eats mynahs in this web, so fewer of them are eaten.

items.q: A graph shows that when the number of snakes in a garden fell, the number of mynahs rose. What is the best explanation?
c: Fewer mynahs were eaten by snakes.
items.e: Fewer predators means more prey survive.

items.q: Siti counted the animals in a school garden: 120 aphids, 15 ladybirds. Why are there more aphids than ladybirds?
c: Each ladybird eats many aphids, and less energy reaches the ladybirds.
items.e: Prey usually outnumber predators.

items.q: Why can a fall in the number of bees affect many animals?
c: Bees pollinate plants that many animals depend on for food.
items.e: Living things depend on each other.

items.q: Look at the food web of a mangrove swamp. Most of the crabs are removed. Which population is most likely to increase at first?
items.e: Only the crab eats mangrove trees in this web, so fewer of them are eaten.

items.q: Why are food chains in real habitats joined into food webs?
c: Most animals eat more than one kind of food.
items.e: Many links.

items.q: Look at the food web of a mangrove swamp. Most of the mudskippers are removed. Which population is most likely to increase at first?
items.e: Only the mudskipper eats snails in this web, so fewer of them are eaten.

items.q: Farmers released ladybirds into a vegetable farm with many aphids. What is the most likely result?
items.e: Ladybirds are predators of aphids.

items.q: Look at the food web of a coral reef. Most of the zooplankton are removed. Which population is most likely to increase at first?
items.e: Only the zooplankton eats phytoplankton in this web, so fewer of them are eaten.

items.q: Look at the food web of a school garden. A disease kills most of the grass. Which population is most likely to decrease first?
items.e: The grasshopper eats only grass in this web, so it loses its food.

items.q: Look at the food web of a coral reef. A disease kills most of the small fish. Which population is most likely to decrease first?
items.e: The squid eats only a small fish in this web, so it loses its food.

items.q: A pupil drew a food chain: grasshopper → grass → mynah. What is wrong?
items.e: Correct: grass → grasshopper → mynah.

items.q: Look at the food web of a coral reef. A disease kills most of the phytoplankton. Which population is most likely to decrease first?
items.e: The zooplankton eats only phytoplankton in this web, so it loses its food.

items.e: Only the heron eats frogs in this web, so fewer of them are eaten.

items.q: Look at the food web of a coral reef. Most of the squid are removed. Which population is most likely to increase at first?

items.e: Only the frog eats dragonfly nymphs in this web, so fewer of them are eaten.

items.q: The number of mosquitoes in a pond fell after guppies were added. Why?
c: Guppies eat adult mosquitoes in the air.
items.e: Guppies are used to control mosquito breeding.

items.q: Look at the food web of a pond. A disease kills most of the algae. Which population is most likely to decrease first?
items.e: The mosquito larva eats only algae in this web, so it loses its food.
